scope: Selected ISO 32000-2:2020 clause 13.2 media-data/timing/player-identification rows only; effective EC3. The audit covers parse/viability and file handoff, not decoding, playback, seeking, screen presentation, or a software-identified media player.

annotations.effect: Table 285 /CT: strikes 'should' and inserts 'shall' in the RFC 2045 content-type conformance sentence.
Amends §13.2.6.1 screen-parameter MH/BE wording only; outside the assigned .6.2/.6.3 clauses and not a blanket alteration to §13.2.5 play parameters.

features.effective_source: D is required and must identify valid media data; a Type-less/unrecognized/non-dictionary-or-stream D is non-viable, simple file specifications are effectively excluded. For embedded file streams, stream Subtype is ignored and CT identifies media type. CT is optional except form XObjects; effective EC3 #257 says its string shall conform to RFC 2045. Form-XObject media is rendered as data, a separate excluded playback behavior.
features.implementation: pdf_model::media reads D/CT, distinguishes embedded/file/URL/form data, uses CT for container and offset handling; viewer-core hands an eligible clip over through Event::Media at the Media restriction level.
features.assertions: Model tests cover simple-file-spec refusal and form-XObject classification; media_viability tests and viewer-core/tests/renditions.rs use a valid video/mp4 embedded stream, check the content type/bytes, viability report and restriction controls. No inspected test independently validates arbitrary CT syntax against RFC 2045.
features.classification: Reader viability/handoff is implemented for supported data sources. #257's syntax requirement is a producer constraint; source does not state a reader recovery verdict for malformed CT. Do not count lack of an RFC-2045 validator as a confirmed reader defect. External paths/URLs are not fetched; embedded data is the supported examined path.

features.effective_source: Media-data MH entries must be honored for viability; BE entries are best effort. Table 286 permissions constrain temporary-file handoff; TF defaults TEMPNEVER, unknown TF reads as TEMPNEVER. MH BU requires honoring the base URL for viability; BE is best effort.
features.implementation: media::clip_data parses permissions, reports base URL and media-player criteria, then the host applies Operation::HandOverMedia. Embedded file temporary-file permissions are a separate policy gate.
features.assertions: viewer-core/tests/renditions.rs checks default restriction behavior, refused TEMPNEVER, permitted TEMPALWAYS, and ask/yes handoff. Existing media-viability tests exercise MH/BE and unhonoured fields.
features.classification: Implemented for viability and handoff policy; does not itself start a player or resolve base URLs.

features.effective_source: D chain must terminate in media clip data; a nonviable child makes section nonviable. B/E define relative offsets; still-image types ignore offsets with no viability effect; time/frame E past end clamps to end with no viability effect; absent markers or out-of-range marker offsets are ignored. MH offsets must be honored at play time for viability; deeper B/E inherit MH treatment. BE entries may be ignored when unsupported.
features.implementation: Walk::clip recurses through section chains; supported embedded containers provide timelines and named markers. The no-player handoff is considered to start at the file beginning and play all of it, so MH offsets that require a nonzero start/interior end are nonviable. Container-independent and unsupported-source limits are reported.
features.assertions: media_viability.rs provides explicit JPEG ignore controls, zero time/frame start controls, negative and nonzero offsets, nested section controls, exact-end/over-end/in-range end comparisons for MP4 and WAVE, marker-present/missing/out-of-range controls, and unsupported/URL/cut-short cases.
features.classification: Well-supported viability implementation for the enumerated embedded container subset. It is not a player seek implementation; that half is excluded. Do not claim all media formats or external sources are understood.

features.effective_source: P is referenced from media rendition; MH parameters must be honored for viability, BE only best effort. Table 291 gives default volume/controller/fit/autoplay/repeat values. D selects intrinsic, infinite, or explicit timespan duration; negative duration is prohibited. If simple duration exceeds intrinsic duration, playback freezes at final state; duration repeats apply as stated.
features.implementation: Media-parameter viability reads MH/BE and duration dictionary. A handoff cannot convey volume, fit, autoplay, repeat or duration choices to its external player; playback/freeze/repetition are not implemented. BE unknown duration subtype is set aside, while an explicit /T whose Table 300 subtype is unrecognized invokes that table’s independent rendition-nonviable rule (ADR 2472).
features.assertions: play_parameters_are_viable_on_their_best_effort_options_and_their_players separates MH from BE. an_unrecognised_timespan_in_a_best_effort_duration_makes_the_rendition_non_viable includes recognized 2.5 seconds, negative/missing fields, unrecognized timespan, duration subtype ignored cases, and MH control.
features.classification: Viability logic is implemented within handoff model. Table 291 playback effects and Table 292's freeze/repeat timing are excluded; tests do not certify playback.

features.effective_source: Offsets are time, frame, or marker; negative time is prohibited, frame numbering begins at zero and negatives are out of range. Timespan subtype shall be S, seconds may be nonintegral and shall not be negative. Unknown subtype explicitly renders the rendition nonviable. Absent or malformed entries are distinct from an unrecognized subtype.
features.implementation: read_offset/read_timespan make those distinctions; a container timeline is consulted for a claimed endpoint or marker only within supported embedded formats.
features.assertions: Tests assert half-second syntax through offset paths, zero/nonzero times, frame 0/negative frame, missing subtype/value, unknown subtype, end boundaries, and marker controls. Tests confirm the report's viability, not that a player later seeks or times playback.
features.classification: Implemented for the supported viability question; actual time/frame seek and duration timing are player behavior excluded by CLAUDE.md principle 5.

features.effective_source: PID required. MH entries must be honored, but the table currently defines none; BE entries need only be honored best effort.
features.implementation: player_info_set_aside removes wrong-shape records, records missing PID and unknown MH entries, validates PID identifier, and ignores BE entries. It does not identify an installed external player.
features.assertions: Tests cover missing PID, unknown/empty MH behavior indirectly, BE syntax in a path whose viability is also decided by unknown handoff identity; no isolated BE-only assertion checks set-aside behavior.
features.classification: Data validation implemented for current handoff. Add an assertion-only regression for BE isolation; no need for a player identity implementation under current exclusion.

features.effective_source: Unknown keys are partially recognized, with processor discretion depending on context; matching compares software name, version range (inclusive/exclusive bounds), and exact OS membership (empty OS matches all). URI scheme is case-insensitive; unknown schemes are non-match; vnd.adobe.swname names are unescaped once and compared case-sensitively. Version arrays compare lexicographically with zero-padding, empty array as infinity; negative values make the identifier nonviable.
features.implementation: For viability, the current handoff/external player has no software identifier and the processor knows no player name/version/OS. The implementation checks identifier structural viability, required U and negative versions, and treats viable identifiers as no match; it does not implement the name URI decode, OS matching or version-range comparison algorithm.
features.assertions: Tests cover unknown keys, missing U, negative L/H and no-player matching behavior. They do not exercise software URI escape/case rules, OS comparisons, LI/HI boundaries, zero-padding, empty-array infinity, or version matching.
features.classification: Do not call full matching implemented. Those comparison branches are currently inapplicable to the declared handoff processor and actual player execution is excluded. If a host later identifies a player or this application as a player, this row must be revisited; existing tests cannot certify the standard algorithm.
